evidence.description: The covenant is an obligation prohibited unless one of the listed exceptions applies; the exceptions are conditions that qualify the operative rule.
evidence.sourceSpan: Create, incur, assume or suffer to exist any Lien upon any of its Property or revenues, whether now owned or hereafter acquired, except for:

evidence.description: The exception for contested taxes and charges is itself conditioned on maintaining adequate reserves, so the permitted-liens treatment depends on that ongoing condition.
evidence.sourceSpan: provided that adequate reserves with respect thereto are maintained on the books of the Parent Borrower or its Subsidiaries, as the case may be, in conformity with GAAP;

evidence.description: The (g) exception for after-acquired property is qualified by two express provisos limiting the property covered and the secured debt amount, so downstream representation of this exception as unconditional would be materially incomplete.
evidence.sourceSpan: provided that (A) no such Lien shall extend to or cover any Property of the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary other than the Property so acquired or financed, and (B) the principal amount of Indebtedness secured by any such Lien shall at no time exceed 80% of the fair market value (as determined in good faith by a Responsible Officer) of such Property at the time it was acquired (by purchase, construction or otherwise);

evidence.description: The catch-all permitted-liens exception is gated by a 'so long as' condition tied to principal amount and fair market value thresholds, making the exception a conditional eligibility carveout.
evidence.sourceSpan: Liens not otherwise permitted by this Section 7.3 so long as neither (i) the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the obligations secured thereby nor (ii) the aggregate fair market value (determined as of the date such Lien is incurred) of the assets subject thereto exceeds (as to the Parent Borrower and all Subsidiaries) the greater of (A) $50,000,000 and (B) 3.0% of Consolidated Total Assets (measured on the date of incurrence of such Liens);

evidence.description: The classification mechanism operates only 'in the event that' the Lien meets criteria from cross-referenced permitted-lien categories, embedding both an event condition and incorporated cross-reference conditions.
evidence.sourceSpan: and (B) in the event that a Lien securing an item of Indebtedness (or any portion thereof) meets the criteria of one or more of the categories of permitted Liens described in Section 7.3(a) through (p), the Parent Borrower shall, in its sole discretion, classify or reclassify, or later divide, classify or reclassify, such Lien securing such item of Indebtedness (or any portion thereof) in any manner that complies with this covenant

findings.sourceEvidence: Section 7.3(g)(ii)(A): 'no such Lien shall extend to or cover any Property of the Parent Borrower or such Subsidiary other than the Property so acquired or financed', read with the opening of clause (g): 'Liens upon real and/or tangible personal Property acquired after the Closing Date ... by the Parent Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries'.
findings.verifierReasoning: In the source, 'such Subsidiary' is an anaphoric reference to the particular Subsidiary that acquired (or financed) the property that is subject to the Lien described in clause (g). The proviso therefore limits the Lien to the property of the Parent Borrower and of that specific Subsidiary; it does not, by its own terms, extend the restriction to all subsidiaries. The proposed IR instead states the rule applies to ANY_SUBSIDIARY. This overbreadth is material: under the source, a Lien that qualifies under (g)(ii) on Subsidiary X's acquired property but also extends to Subsidiary Y's separately-permitted property would not violate clause (A) because Y is not 'such Subsidiary'; the proposed IR would treat that as a violation of this rule. The IR also substitutes 'BORROWER' for the defined term 'Parent Borrower' and does not carry forward the antecedent limitation that 'such Lien' means a Lien within clause (g)(ii) securing Section 7.2-permitted Indebtedness.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed IR contains no condition or exception representing the 80% fair-market-value limit; its conditions array is empty and the rule's sufficiency is 'COMPLETE'.
findings.sourceEvidence: Section 7.3(g)(ii)(B): 'the principal amount of Indebtedness secured by any such Lien shall at no time exceed 80% of the fair market value (as determined in good faith by a Responsible Officer) of such Property at the time it was acquired (by purchase, construction or otherwise);'
findings.verifierReasoning: The source's proviso to the (g) exception is a two-part conjunctive condition: (A) limits the property covered by the Lien, and (B) limits the secured principal to 80% of the property's fair market value at acquisition. The proposed IR represents only (A) and marks itself COMPLETE. If the IR is consumed as the representation of the (g)(ii) proviso or of the scope of the exception, a Lien that covers only the acquired property but secures more than 80% of FMV would appear compliant even though it fails condition (B). Because the IR's sourceSectionRef is expressly limited to '7.3(g)(ii)(A)', the omission may be outside the intended representation; I therefore mark this UNCERTAIN rather than MATERIAL, but it is a real gap in the complete proviso that the source itself presents as a single 'provided that' unit ending in 'and'.
